topics.title: Algebra 2: Quadratic Expressions
topics.subject: mathematics
outcomes: Recognise equivalent quadratic expressions. (k, u, s)
Solve quadratic equations where the quadratic expression can be factorised. (k, s)

body.text: To expand (x+3)(x+4), multiply every term in the first bracket by every term in the second: x*x + x*4 + 3*x + 3*4 = x^2 + 4x + 3x + 12 = x^2 + 7x + 12. Notice the coefficient of x (7) is the sum of 3 and 4, and the constant (12) is their product — this pattern is the key to factorising.
To factorise x^2 + 7x + 12, find two numbers that multiply to give 12 (the constant) and add to give 7 (the coefficient of x): 3 and 4 work, since 3x4=12 and 3+4=7. So x^2 + 7x + 12 = (x+3)(x+4).

A perfect square like (x+5)^2 expands to x^2 + 10x + 25 — the middle term is always twice the product of x and the constant. To solve a factorisable quadratic equation, factorise it and use the fact that if two things multiply to give zero, one of them must be zero. Solve x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0: this factorises to (x-2)(x-3) = 0, so x=2 or x=3.
